title: The audit-log stream carries actor, target, before and after fields per line with the ambient correlation identifier for consumer surfaces to join
asA: operator of a consuming blueprint (application-admin-console) rendering an audit-log surface
iWant: every audit event the applying application emits to land on the same shared logger stream with actor, target, before, after and correlationId fields on the top-level object
soThat: the audit surface can read the stream directly, join each row to its originating request via the correlation identifier, and use the shared redaction and level-filter pipeline without a per-consumer adapter

acceptanceCriteria.description: An audit event emission at info with a payload carrying { actor: 'principal:1', target: 'role:2', before: 'reader', after: 'admin' } produces one stdout line whose parsed object holds those four fields at the top level alongside message, level, timestamp, correlationId, environment, serviceName and serviceVersion; the correlationId equals the ambient request context's value.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a running application in an ambient request context with correlationId 'req-777' and a caller issuing logger.info('role.granted', { actor: 'principal:1', target: 'role:2', before: 'reader', after: 'admin' })
acceptanceCriteria.when: the emission passes through the factory
acceptanceCriteria.then: stdout carries one line, JSON.parse yields an object with actor === 'principal:1', target === 'role:2', before === 'reader', after === 'admin', correlationId === 'req-777' and the shared minimum field set present
acceptanceCriteria.templateFillIns: The applying agent sets the elicited environment, serviceName and serviceVersion on the boot-identity-fields elicit; the AC substitutes those values for the illustrative literals.

acceptanceCriteria.description: An audit event emitted at debug with the elicited minimum-log-level set to info produces no stdout line, so the audit stream in production does not carry sub-threshold audit noise.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a running application with minimum-log-level info and a caller issuing logger.debug('role.hover', { actor: 'principal:1', target: 'role:2', before: 'reader', after: 'reader' })
acceptanceCriteria.then: stdout carries no line for this emission
acceptanceCriteria.templateFillIns: The applying agent sets the elicited minimum-log-level per environment; the AC substitutes the elicited threshold for the illustrative info.

acceptanceCriteria.description: An audit event whose actor value has category pii.email at the caller-side has that field replaced with [REDACTED:pii.email] on the emitted line; the caller-side object still holds the original address.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a running application configured with the recommended redaction defaults and a caller issuing logger.info('login.success', { actor: 'alice@example.test', 'actor.pii.email': 'alice@example.test' })
acceptanceCriteria.when: the emission passes through the redaction boundary
acceptanceCriteria.then: the stdout line's `actor.pii.email` field value equals [REDACTED:pii.email] and the caller-side object still holds 'alice@example.test'

acceptanceCriteria.description: The blueprint's guide 'Known mechanism-reach gaps' section names the class of a bare console.log or bare stdout write bypassing the factory. This AC verifies that the guide states the gap and names at least one project-side workaround (an ESLint rule or a build-time grep gate) that a consuming project can adopt to close it; the blueprint does not itself supply the gate.
acceptanceCriteria.then: the guide names the mechanism-reach gap explicitly and states at least one project-side workaround by name
